core_thesis: Synthetic supervision alone yields a strong pallet keypoint estimator without any real pose label. Self-training on unlabeled target RGB increases observed nighttime detection coverage, while the overall detection difference is not statistically resolved, and the full consistency variant achieves the best observed AUROC and FPR95 among the frozen adaptation arms. Under a controlled exposure-matched protocol it does not improve fine keypoint localisation over the synthetic-only model, and adding projective and equivariant consistency to the pseudo-label selection rule does not recover a localisation gain. Post-hoc diagnostics show the limitation is not explained by any single filtering implementation. These observations are consistent with a teacher-quality bottleneck; the study does not establish one.

population.name: PAPER_EVAL
population.consequence: no number computed on this population may be called held-out or independently confirmed

supported_claims.claim: Synthetic-only supervision is already a strong real-domain baseline.
Self-training on unlabeled target RGB increases observed nighttime detection coverage; the overall detection difference is not statistically resolved.
mandatory_caveats: The gain is NOT attributable to the geometry filter: naive self-training reaches 0.960 unaided and confidence-only reaches 0.980, higher than the full filter.
The overall detection difference between R0 and the full filter is not separated from noise: p_better 0.121 frame-level, 0.244 session-clustered.
N = 50 must be printed with any use of this subgroup.

supported_claims.claim: The full consistency variant achieves the best observed AUROC and FPR95 among the frozen adaptation arms.
supported_claims.note: This is the only axis on which the proposed filter is best of all seven arms. It is stated as best observed, not as an established improvement: the ranking metrics carry no bootstrap interval in the artifacts.

supported_claims.claim: Fine 2D keypoint localisation does not improve over the synthetic-only model.

evidence.unit: original-image pixels, median of supervised keypoints

supported_claims.permitted_phrasing: self-training did not improve localisation; the direction is a small degradation, frame-level significant and not session-level significant
supported_claims.forbidden_phrasing: self-training harms localisation (without the session-level caveat)

metric_semantics.definition: Fine keypoint localisation is evaluated in the 2D image plane using supervised keypoint error in original-image pixels.
metric_semantics.disclaimer: These values are not 6D pose errors and must not be interpreted as yaw, translation, ADD, or operational alignment accuracy.

supported_claims.claim: Geometry-based filtering shows no clear additional downstream localisation gain over confidence-only selection.
The pseudo-label selection signals are not random.
Reliability weighting improved the quality of the labels the student saw and did not improve student localisation.
Near-square projections carry a 90-degree semantic-axis ambiguity that is one of the failure modes.
supported_claims.note: judge such frames by maximum corner error; the distribution is bimodal and the median hides the failure

forbidden_sentences: our geometry filter improves pose accuracy
geometry filtering provides a clear downstream gain
our geometric filter improves nighttime detection
no real annotation was used anywhere
primary pose metric (for the pixel metric)
we switched to NME because px was unfair

pose_metrics.example_allowed: keypoints are converted to a 6D pose using PnP
pose_metrics.blocker_is_algorithmic: best measured axis selector 0.65 against a gate of 0.95; further manual annotation would not open these slots

proposed_method_identity.rule: V3-B is never presented as the proposed method, and V1 frozen arms and V3-B are never given the same evidence level

terminology.box_ap50 / box_ap50_95 / auroc / fpr95: the evaluator's own names; there is no metric called ranking AP
terminology.pooled supervised keypoint median error: never unqualified corner error; never reprojection error
terminology.NME: post-hoc scale-normalised diagnostic; never a frozen or primary metric

citation_state.rule: no citation may be fabricated; Related Work must be written against literature the authors actually consult
